_comment: FPVLink system configuration — edit this file and restart the service to apply changes.

device._comment: Human-readable device identity. Version follows semver.
device.name: FPVLink

capture._comment: USB capture layer configuration. IMPORTANT: the usb_vid/usb_pid/interface/ep_out/ep_in fields below describe the V1/V2 path only — the Pi acting as USB HOST to Goggles V1/V2, which is what capture/v1v2.py and capture/host_capture.py drive. They are NOT the Goggles 2/3/Integra/N3 path: there the roles are reversed, the Pi is the gadget and the goggles are the host, and the identity the Pi presents lives in DESCRIPTOR_TEMPLATE in capture/goggles2.py. Do not expect changes here to affect Goggles 2. strict_duml_ack and oneshot_app_register below DO apply to the Goggles 2 path.
capture._goggles_model_comment: Which goggles variant to expect on USB. Options: 'v1v2' (DJI FPV Goggles V1/V2), 'goggles2' (DJI Goggles 2 / Goggles Integra), 'auto' (try both, slower init).
capture._interface_comment: USB interface number carrying the video bulk endpoints. V1/V2 path only. Override per-run with v1v2.py --iface.
capture._ep_out_comment: USB bulk-OUT endpoint number (host → device, for control commands).
capture._ep_in_comment: USB bulk-IN endpoint number (device → host, receives raw H.265 stream).
capture._usb_vid_comment: USB Vendor ID to look for on the bus (0x2CA3 = DJI). V1/V2 path only. Accepts 0x-prefixed hex or a decimal number; anything unparseable falls back to 0x2CA3. Override per-run with v1v2.py --vid.
capture._usb_pid_comment: USB Product ID. 'auto' (default) accepts any PID under the vendor ID above. Set a specific value like '0x001F' to lock to one model. V1/V2 path only. Override per-run with v1v2.py --pid.
capture._read_timeout_ms_comment: Milliseconds to wait for a USB bulk read before timing out and retrying.
capture._max_packet_size_comment: Maximum USB transfer size in bytes per read call. Larger = fewer syscalls. Must be a multiple of the USB wMaxPacketSize (usually 512 or 1024).
capture._strict_duml_ack_comment: FIX (validated on hardware 2026-07-31) for 'goggles menus glitch / transmission settings won't change while USB-C is attached'. true (default) = only answer DUML packets addressed to us (dst=0x02) that are requests (cmd_type bit7 clear) and actually asked for an ACK (bit6 set), always replying as ourselves. false = legacy: reply to EVERY packet on the control port, forging src_id from the packet's dst_id — i.e. answering on behalf of internal goggles components, which collides with their real replies. Measured: legacy needed 2808 forged ACKs per session and the menus were unusable; with this on the handshake completes with 0 ACKs, video starts normally (60.4fps / 9.5Mbps / 36ms at full power) and the menus work. Suppressed replies log at DEBUG so a broken handshake names what the goggles were waiting on. Set false to roll back instantly (restart capture; no redeploy).
capture._oneshot_app_register_comment: MITIGATION, same symptom. Keep-alive 'Command B' is an app-registration ('APP' payload) telling the goggles a phone app attached. false (default) = legacy: resend every 5s forever, so the goggles see an app re-attaching for the whole session. true = send only while video is NOT arriving — still starts the stream, still restarts it after a >1s stall, but stops nagging once it is running. WARNING: Command B is load-bearing for starting video (a past change to it produced zero video); this alters only WHEN it is sent, never its bytes. Set false to roll back.

pipeline._bitrate_kbps_comment: Target encode bitrate in kilobits per second for streaming outputs (SRT/RTMP).
pipeline._codec_comment: Output codec for streaming branches. Only 'h264' is currently supported. 'h265' output is planned for a future release.
pipeline._use_hardware_comment: If true, use Rockchip MPP (mppvideodec / mppvideoenc) for decode+encode. If false, or if rkmpp plugin is unavailable, falls back to avdec_h265 + x264enc (software — high CPU, higher latency).
pipeline._latency_mode_comment: Preset that tunes internal queue depths and encoder settings. Options: 'low' (2-buffer queues, zero-latency encoder tune — ideal for FPV), 'balanced' (4-buffer queues, moderate quality), 'quality' (8-buffer queues, higher quality encoder settings — not recommended for real-time).
pipeline._keyframe_interval_comment: Encoder keyframe interval in frames. At 30fps, 60 = 2-second GOP. Shorter GOPs improve seek latency but increase bitrate.
pipeline._decode_disable_error_comment: Pass disable-error=true to mppvideodec so non-fatal decoding errors (e.g. partial NAL units) don't abort the pipeline.

outputs._comment: Output destinations. Each can be independently enabled or disabled.

srt._comment: SRT (Secure Reliable Transport) streaming. Low-latency, UDP-based, tolerates packet loss. Ideal for local network or point-to-point IP links.
srt._url_comment: Full SRT URI, e.g. 'srt://192.168.1.50:9000' for caller mode or 'srt://:9000' for listener mode.
srt._latency_ms_comment: SRT end-to-end latency in milliseconds. Lower = less delay, higher = more resilient to packet loss. 100ms is a good balance for local WiFi.
srt._wait_for_connection_comment: If false, srtsink won't block the pipeline when no receiver is connected. Set true if you want pipeline start to wait for a viewer.

rtmp._comment: RTMP streaming for platforms like YouTube Live, Twitch, or a local NGINX-RTMP server.
rtmp._url_comment: RTMP base URL, e.g. 'rtmp://a.rtmp.youtube.com/live2'. The stream key from stream_key or from STREAM_KEY_YOUTUBE env var is appended automatically.
rtmp._stream_key_comment: RTMP stream key. Leave blank to read from STREAM_KEY_YOUTUBE / STREAM_KEY_TWITCH environment variables (more secure — keys not stored in this file).
rtmp._buffer_ms_comment: Internal RTMP output buffer in milliseconds. Increase if you see 'rtmpsink: buffer underflow' warnings.

rtsp._comment: RTSP server (future feature — not yet implemented in v0.1.0).
rtsp._port_comment: RTSP server port. Standard RTSP port is 554 but that requires root; 8554 works as a non-root user.
rtsp._path_comment: RTSP mount path. Full URL will be rtsp://device-ip:8554/live.

hdmi._comment: Direct HDMI output via KMS/DRM. Zero-copy hardware decoded feed.
hdmi._connector_id_comment: HDMI connector ID. 217 targets the dedicated HDMI0 out. Set explicitly to target specific HDMI port.
hdmi._plane_id_comment: DRM plane on connector 217's CRTC (89). 194 is a native-NV12 video overlay, so the decoder's NV12 reaches the panel with no software videoconvert. Auto-select picks RGB-only plane 178, which forces a CPU-heavy convert. Currently hardcoded in capture/pipeline.py (KMS_PLANE_ID); this field documents it.

ndi._comment: NDI (Network Device Interface) output. Broadcasts a low-latency NDI source on the LAN, auto-discovered by OBS, vMix, and NDI Studio Monitor. Taps the decoded NV12 feed directly (no color convert). Toggling this restarts the pipeline to apply (~3s standby blip).
ndi.name: FPVLink
ndi._name_comment: NDI source name shown to receivers on the network.

standby._comment: The card shown on HDMI whenever there is no live signal. Changing this restarts the pipeline to apply (~3s standby blip), so change it before the drone is live.
standby._active_card_comment: One of: 'grounded' (branded still), 'grounded_anim' (the same card animated), 'bars' (SMPTE-style test pattern), 'black' (sync black). Ids are defined in STANDBY_CARDS in capture/pipeline.py; an unknown id falls back to 'grounded'.
standby._animated_comment: 'grounded_anim' is a 60-frame 6s loop at 10fps from capture/cards/anim/grounded/. Motion is a liveness signal: a still card looks identical to a crashed box on a downstream monitor. It costs ~6% of one core continuously (the standby branch runs even while live, which is what keeps the fallback to standby instant). If its frames are missing or gapped the pipeline logs why and falls back to 'grounded'.

web._comment: Embedded web UI / control API server (Node.js Express). If FPVLINK_PASSWORD is set in system/fpvlink.env the dashboard asks for it; if it is blank the dashboard is OPEN to anyone who can reach the port and the journal warns on every boot. The service starts either way — a missing password never stops the box working. Requests from 127.0.0.1 are always exempt so on-box scripts keep working.
web._port_comment: TCP port for the web server and dashboard. FPVLINK_PORT in system/fpvlink.env overrides it. Needs a service restart. Values outside 1-65535 are ignored and 8080 is used; journalctl names both the port and where it came from at startup.
web._allow_remote_comment: true (default) = the dashboard listens on every interface, which is what you want: the whole point is reaching it from a phone or laptop, including over the field AP. false = bind 127.0.0.1 only, reachable from the box itself and nothing else — useful for a box you administer over SSH and never want exposed. Changing this needs a service restart. Only an explicit false binds loopback; a missing key means all interfaces, because a box that silently went unreachable would be worse than the exposure this prevents. The startup line in journalctl always names the address it bound to.
web._session_secret_comment: NOT READ FROM HERE. Session signing is configured with FPVLINK_SESSION_SECRET in system/fpvlink.env, not from config.json — secrets do not belong in a file the dashboard itself can rewrite via POST /api/config. Kept only so the shape of the config does not change under anyone who already edited it.

network._prefer_ethernet_comment: If true, SRT and RTMP traffic is routed via the Ethernet interface when available, preferring it over WiFi for stability.
network._srt_port_comment: Local UDP port for the SRT listener (when this device acts as the SRT server). Opened in the firewall by the setup script.
network._srt_interface_comment: Bind SRT listener to a specific interface (e.g. 'eth0'). Leave blank to bind to all interfaces.

logging._level_comment: Log verbosity. Options: 'error', 'warn', 'info', 'debug'. Can be overridden with LOG_LEVEL env var. Use 'debug' to see full GStreamer pipeline strings.
logging._gst_debug_comment: GStreamer debug level (GST_DEBUG). 0=none, 1=error, 2=warn, 3=fixme, 4=info, 5=debug. Passed as environment variable to the Python process.
logging._file_comment: Optional path to write logs to a file in addition to systemd journal. Leave empty to log to journal only.
